issue.title: feat(router): centralize localized route error handling
issue.body:
<!--
  PR body draft for divine-mobile branch fix/3371-centralize-localized-route-error-handling
-->

## Description

Centralizes localized “bad route” UX behind a shared screen and wires **GoRouter** so unknown URLs show the same layout as other routing guardrails.

- **`RouteErrorScreen`** (`mobile/lib/router/route_error_screen.dart`) — reusable full-screen scaffold: **VineTheme** background, **`DiVineAppBar`**, localized title (defaults to **`routeErrorTitle`**), **`message`**, optional back affordance (**`showBackButton`**, **`onBackPressed`** with default **`context.pop`**).
- **`GoRouter.errorBuilder`** — **`RouteErrorScreen(message: context.l10n.routeUnknownPath)`** for paths that do not match any route.
- **`app_router.dart`** — all previous inline **`Scaffold`** route-error branches now delegate to **`RouteErrorScreen`**, preserving existing **`context.l10n.*`** strings for invalid IDs, hashtags, pools without data, etc. Removes the stray **`package:divine_ui/divine_ui.dart`** import from the router module (widgets live under **`route_error_screen.dart`**).
- **Localization:** new **`routeUnknownPath`** in **`app_en.arb`** (with **`@routeUnknownPath`** metadata) plus the same key in **all 16 non-English** **`app_*.arb`** files; **`flutter gen-l10n`** outputs updated under **`mobile/lib/l10n/generated/`**.
- **Tests:** **`mobile/test/router/route_error_routing_test.dart`** covers (1) navigation to an unknown path → **`errorBuilder`** shows **`routeUnknownPath`**, (2) **`go`** to pooled fullscreen route without **`extra`** → **`RouteErrorScreen`** with **`routeNoVideosToDisplay`** (stable integration surface; empty path-parameter URLs are not relied on because **go_router** normalizes some segments).
- **Misc:** **`notification_repository`** — drops obsolete **`// ignore: avoid_equals_and_hash_code_on_mutable_classes`** comments on **`_VideoGroupKey`** now that the class is annotated **`@immutable`** (no behavior change).

issue.title: feat(l10n): add Filipino (fil) localization
issue.body:
Closes #4098

## Summary

- Adds Filipino (`fil`) as the 18th supported app locale to serve the Philippines (now the 4th most popular country)
- Translates 1711 message keys to natural Manila Filipino / Taglish; the existing `_knownUntranslatedDebt` set (300 keys) falls back to English
- Registers the locale in all 4 platform layers gated by `test/l10n/platform_locale_declarations_test.dart`

## Translation approach

Strings translated **per-string** with explicit instructions against regex word-substitution (a first attempt produced broken Taglish like "Maghanap failed", "Pumili color", "Nabigo to update video" and was discarded). Translators were briefed on `brand-guidelines/TONE_OF_VOICE.md` (Tone Dial — in-app UI: Rebel low, Playful high) and matched the conventions established by the existing 16-locale parity pass (commit b5a666570).

Conventions used:
- Informal pronouns (`mo` / `ka` / `iyong` / `nila`)
- `i-` prefix for English-rooted action verbs (`I-share`, `I-edit`, `I-publish`)
- Tech and brand terms retained in English (Divine, Nostr, NIP-05, relay, video, feed, npub, nsec, etc.) — matches how Filipino mobile apps actually localize (Facebook, Lazada, Shopee)
- All `{placeholder}` tokens, `\n` newlines, and ICU plurals preserved verbatim

## Locale registration

| Layer | File |
|---|---|
| Dart picker | `mobile/lib/services/locale_preference_service.dart` |
| Generated AppLocalizations | `mobile/lib/l10n/generated/app_localizations.dart` (regenerated by `flutter gen-l10n`) |
| Android per-app language config | `mobile/android/app/src/main/res/xml/locales_config.xml` |
| iOS Info.plist | `mobile/ios/Runner/Info.plist` (`CFBundleLocalizations`) |
| Xcode project | `mobile/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (`knownRegions`) |

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` — green (key parity holds for new locale)
- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/platform_locale_declarations_test.dart` — green (all 4 platform configs include `fil`)
- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/l10n_test.dart` — green (16 cases, including plurals and parameterized strings)
- [x] `flutter test test/services/locale_preference_service_test.dart` — green (picker exposes `fil`)
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — `No issues found!`
- [ ] Manual: switch device locale to Filipino, verify UI strings render in Taglish and unsupported strings fall back to English
- [ ] Spot-check by a native Filipino speaker (mid-week pass) to flag any awkward phrasings before launch

issue.title: Localize hardcoded semantic labels in feed overlay and video item
issue.body:
The `/check-l10n` skill flagged 6 user-visible English literals in the feed overlay / video item code paths that are not routed through `context.l10n`. They are pre-existing (not introduced by any current branch) and surface every time these files are touched.

Per `localization.md`, all user-facing strings — including semantic labels read by screen readers — must use the l10n system. Per `accessibility.md`, semantic labels are accessibility-critical and must be translated.

## Findings (from `python3 .claude/skills/check-l10n/scan_strings.py`)

- `mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_mode_switch.dart:85` — `[label-arg]` `'For You'`
- `mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_mode_switch.dart:119` — `[label-arg]` `'Feed mode: $label'`
- `mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay.dart:300` — `[label-arg]` `'Video author: $displayName'`
- `mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay.dart:410` — `[semanticLabel-arg]` `'Author avatar'`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_feed_item/video_feed_item.dart:1515` — `[semanticLabel-arg]` `'Author avatar'`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_feed_item/video_feed_item.dart:1545` — `[label-arg]` `'Video author: $displayName'`

## Suggested ARB keys

- `feedModeForYou` → `"For You"` (likely already exists — check first)
- `feedModeSemanticLabel` → `"Feed mode: {label}"` (placeholder)
- `videoAuthorSemanticLabel` → `"Video author: {displayName}"` (placeholder)
- `videoAuthorAvatarSemanticLabel` → `"Author avatar"`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 6 lines route through `context.l10n.<key>`
- [ ] New keys added to `app_en.arb` with `@key` metadata for placeholders
- [ ] `flutter gen-l10n` run and regenerated files committed
- [ ] New keys either translated for ship-locales or added to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` in `mobile/test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` with attribution
- [ ] `flutter test test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` passes
- [ ] `python3 .claude/skills/check-l10n/scan_strings.py mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_mode_switch.dart mobile/lib/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay.dart mobile/lib/widgets/video_feed_item/video_feed_item.dart` exits 0

review.body: This closes the hardcoded semantics debt cleanly: the affected feed-mode and video-author labels now go through `AppLocalizations`, all shipped locales carry the new keys, generated l10n stays in sync, and the widget tests assert through localized lookups instead of hardcoded English.

issue.title: fix: invite count not updating after generation
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3771 -- invite notification card shows stale count after generating an invite code.

**Root cause:** `availableInviteCount` in `InviteStatusState` summed `remaining + unclaimedCodes.length`. When an invite is generated, the server decrements `remaining` by 1 and adds a new unclaimed code (+1), so the sum was invariant. The BlocBuilder saw no change and the UI appeared stuck.

**Fix:** Redefine `availableInviteCount` in the model to return `remaining` only. Generation is treated as the proxy for handoff -- it's the only discrete, reliable signal (share sheet completion, copy actions, screenshots are all uncapturable). All surfaces (notifications card, settings badge) use the model getters, so they stay consistent.

**Additional fix found in manual testing:** After generating all invites, the Settings invite button disappeared entirely because it gated on `hasAvailableInvites` (remaining > 0). Users need to access their generated codes to re-share them. Added `hasInviteActivity` getter (remaining > 0 OR any codes exist) for the settings entry point. Count badge hides at zero remaining, but the button stays visible. Notification card still disappears at zero -- that's a generation prompt, not a code retrieval path.

## Changes

- `invite_status_state.dart`: `availableInviteCount` returns `remaining` only; new `hasInviteActivity` getter for settings visibility
- `settings_screen.dart`: gate button on `hasInviteActivity`, hide count badge when remaining is 0
- `notifications_screen.dart`: no net change (reverted per-screen patches, uses model getters)
- Tests updated to match new semantics

## Diagnosis

| Step | remaining | unclaimedCodes | old availableInviteCount | new availableInviteCount |
|------|-----------|----------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Initial (5 invites) | 5 | 0 | 5 | 5 |
| Generate 1 | 4 | 1 | 5 (unchanged!) | 4 |
| Generate all 5 | 0 | 5 | 5 (unchanged!) | 0 |

## Test plan

- [x] Generate an invite code, confirm notification card count decrements
- [x] Verify settings badge shows same count as notification card
- [x] Use all remaining invites, confirm notification card disappears
- [x] Use all remaining invites, confirm settings badge count disappears
- [x] Use all remaining invites, confirm settings Invites button stays visible (no count badge)
- [x] Tap into invites screen from settings at zero remaining, confirm codes are accessible
- [x] Pull-to-refresh on notifications tab, confirm count reflects server state
- [x] Switch tabs and return, confirm count persists correctly

comment.body:
Closing this PR rather than merging it.

Re-reviewing the current branch against `origin/main`, the invite-count behavior this PR was addressing has already shipped to main:
- `InviteStatusState.availableInviteCount` now uses `remaining`
- `hasInviteActivity` exists on main
- Settings still shows the invites entry when there is invite activity, but hides the numeric badge when `remaining == 0`
- Notifications tests on main already reflect the `remaining == 0` behavior

What is left on this branch is no longer the core fix. The remaining diff is stale drift in settings files that would revert newer mainline changes if merged, including:
- localized settings titles back to hardcoded English
- the Badges tile removal
- newer integrated-apps routing behavior

So under the current bar, this PR is not something to approve or merge. The substantive invite-count change is already on main, and the remaining branch diff is regression risk.

If we still want a different event boundary for invites — for example decrementing on explicit handoff/share instead of generation — that should be a fresh follow-up from current `main`, because that is now a separate product/design change rather than unfinished work in this branch.

issue.title: fix(security): iOS per-frame origin attestation for Nostr bridge
issue.body:
## Description

Closes #3764.

### Background

The nonce gate shipped in #3759 is the effective immediate defence against iframe abuse of the Nostr bridge. Issue #3764 tracks the longer-term platform-layer improvement: per-frame origin attestation, so the host can distinguish top-level pages from subframes at the platform boundary — not just via the JS-side `window.top !== window.self` guard.

The investigation documented in [this comment](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/3764#issuecomment-4375621169) found that `webview_flutter_wkwebview` 3.24.1 truncates `WKScriptMessage` to `name` and `body` only — `frameInfo` is absent from the pigeon definition. However, the package ships a stable public external API (`FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI`) specifically for app-level native code to look up a `WKWebView` by its Dart-assigned integer identifier, enabling the local plugin approach implemented here.

### What changed

**New: `mobile/ios/Runner/NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.swift`**

Swift plugin with two classes:
- `NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin` — registers a `MethodChannel` (`co.openvine/nostr_bridge_attestation`) and `EventChannel` (`co.openvine/nostr_bridge_attestation/events`). On `attach(webViewId)`, it calls `FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI.webView(forIdentifier:withPluginRegistry:)` to obtain the live `WKWebView`, removes the pigeon-managed `WKScriptMessageHandler` for `divineSandboxBridge`, and installs its own. On `detach`, it removes the handler.
- `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler` — the replacement handler. In `userContentController(_:didReceive:)` it reads `message.frameInfo.isMainFrame` (a native `WKScriptMessage` field unavailable to Dart via pigeon) and delivers `{message, isMainFrame}` to Dart via the `EventChannel` sink. Origin host/port/scheme are intentionally **not** forwarded — `isMainFrame` is the structural signal this layer needs, and narrowing the contract keeps the security surface minimal. The native test `testEventPayloadHasOnlyMessageAndIsMainFrame` pins this contract so it can't silently regress.

The `addJavaScriptChannel("divineSandboxBridge")` call remains: it installs the `WKUserScript` alias `window.divineSandboxBridge = webkit.messageHandlers.divineSandboxBridge`, which continues to route correctly after the handler swap. Only the handler object is replaced, not the JS-visible name.

**`mobile/ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift`**

Calls `NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.setup(messenger:pluginRegistry:)` after `GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register` — ordering matters because `FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI` requires `WebViewFlutterPlugin` to already be registered.

**`mobile/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`**

Four entries added (`PBXBuildFile`, `PBXFileReference`, group child, Sources build phase) so the new Swift file compiles without a manual Xcode step.

**`mobile/lib/screens/apps/nostr_app_sandbox_screen.dart`**

- `_activateNativeAttestation(controller)` — called during `_configureAndLoadController` on iOS only. Sends `attach(webViewId)` to the Swift plugin, then subscribes to the `EventChannel`. Falls back silently if the channel is not available (tests, macOS, etc.).
- `_handleAttestedEvent(event)` — rejects `isMainFrame: false` with `subframe_rejected` before the nonce check runs. Main-frame events are forwarded to the existing `_handleBridgeMessage`, which applies the nonce gate and policy as before.
- `dispose()` — cancels the stream subscription and fires `detach`.
- `@visibleForTesting onAttestedEventHandlerReady` — exposes `_handleAttestedEvent` to tests without requiring a real WebView.

Android is **unchanged** — nonce gate remains the effective defence on Android. Platform-level parity (`WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener`) is tracked in #4105.

### Reproducing the gap this closes

With only the nonce gate (#3759):
1. Open an approved app (e.g. Primal).
2. The app embeds a same-origin `<iframe>` whose source is attacker-controlled (e.g. via XSS or a compromised CDN asset).
3. The iframe cannot call `window.nostr.*` (bootstrap refuses in non-main frames) — but it can call `window.webkit.messageHandlers.divineSandboxBridge.postMessage(...)` directly.
4. Without a valid nonce the host rejects it (`subframe_or_unauthorized`). The nonce is scoped to IIFE closure so the iframe cannot read it from the parent.
5. The nonce gate is therefore the real blocking control on iOS today — but it is a cryptographic/logical control, not a platform-level structural control.

With this PR, step 3 is also rejected at the platform level: `WKScriptMessage.frameInfo.isMainFrame` is `false` for any message posted from an iframe, and the host denies it with `subframe_rejected` before the nonce check even runs.

### Test plan

**Automated (all pass locally):**

| Test | What it proves |
|------|----------------|
| `rejects non-main-frame events with subframe_rejected` | Platform-level denial fires for any `isMainFrame: false` message |
| `rejects non-main-frame events even when nonce is valid` | Subframe denial is unconditional — valid nonce doesn't help |
| `forwards main-frame events to _handleBridgeMessage` | Attested main-frame calls reach the nonce gate + policy |
| `main-frame events with wrong nonce still hit the nonce gate` | Frame attestation does not bypass the nonce check |
| `non-main-frame event with unparseable message emits subframe_rejected with unknown id` | Graceful handling of malformed payloads from subframes |

```
flutter test test/screens/apps/nostr_app_sandbox_screen_test.dart
# 34 passed (29 existing + 5 new)
flutter analyze lib/screens/apps/ test/screens/apps/
# No issues found
```

**Manual (on device):**
- Open an approved Nostr app and verify `window.nostr.getPublicKey()` still resolves.
- In Safari Web Inspector, inject `window.webkit.messageHandlers.divineSandboxBridge.postMessage(JSON.stringify({id:"x",method:"getPublicKey",args:{},nonce:"anything"}))` from an iframe context and verify the response contains `subframe_rejected`.

### Follow-ups

- Android per-frame origin attestation parity — #4105.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔒 Security hardening (defence-in-depth; does not change observable app behaviour for legitimate main-frame traffic)

issue.title: test(apps): add end-to-end EventChannel coverage for iOS frame attestation
issue.body:
## Summary
PR #3979 added native unit tests for the Swift attestation policy/payload and Dart tests for `_handleAttestedEvent`, but there is still no end-to-end test that exercises the full `WKScriptMessage -> Swift handler -> EventChannel -> Dart` path.

## Why
The current Dart tests use the `onAttestedEventHandlerReady` seam, which proves Dart-side behaviour but not the native-to-Dart hop. This is a security boundary and deserves at least one integration test that does not trust the seam.

## Scope
- add an integration test using `package:integration_test`
- load fixture HTML with a main frame and iframe
- assert the Dart side observes `subframe_rejected` for iframe-originated bridge traffic

issue.title: test(apps): add end-to-end EventChannel coverage for iOS frame attestation
issue.body:
## Summary
PR #3979 added native unit tests for the Swift attestation policy/payload and Dart tests for `_handleAttestedEvent`, but there is still no end-to-end test that exercises the full `WKScriptMessage -> Swift handler -> EventChannel -> Dart` path.

## Why
The current Dart tests use the `onAttestedEventHandlerReady` seam, which proves Dart-side behaviour but not the native-to-Dart hop. This is a security boundary and deserves at least one integration test that does not trust the seam.

## Scope
- add an integration test using `package:integration_test`
- load fixture HTML with a main frame and iframe
- assert the Dart side observes `subframe_rejected` for iframe-originated bridge traffic
- verify main-frame traffic still reaches the bridge path

## Context
Follow-up from PR #3979.

issue.title: build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation RunnerTests
issue.body:
## Summary
The iOS Nostr bridge attestation work added native Swift coverage in `mobile/ios/RunnerTests/RunnerTests.swift`, but `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` is still Ubuntu-only, so these tests do not gate PRs today.

## Why
This is a security-sensitive boundary. Regressions in `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` or `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` should fail CI, not rely on a contributor remembering to run `xcodebuild test` locally.

## Scope
- add a macOS job to `mobile_ci.yaml`
- run `xcodebuild test -scheme Runner -only-testing:RunnerTests` (or the narrow equivalent the project wants)
- make the lane required for PRs touching the mobile app

## Context
Follow-up from PR #3979.

comment.body:
Re-review on `98b979e20020f25fa447c4134815bf7d1cc6e1e1`.

This is close, but it is not ready to merge under the current bar: no new tech debt going forward, and cleanup of existing debt where we are already touching the area.

The substantive feature work looks solid. The remaining blockers are focused and fixable:

1. New l10n debt was added and is currently breaking CI.
- `app_en.arb` adds 4 new keys:
  - `bugReportAttachImages`
  - `bugReportImagesCount`
  - `bugReportRemoveImage`
  - `bugReportUploadFailed`
- `app_am.arb` and `app_bg.arb` do not define those keys.
- That is why `arb_consistency_test.dart` is failing, and it also explains the stale generated localization outputs.
- Please do not add these to `_knownUntranslatedDebt`. These are new keys introduced by this PR, so they need to land translated.
- Required fix:
  - add the 4 keys to `app_am.arb` and `app_bg.arb`
  - run `flutter gen-l10n`
  - commit the regenerated `app_localizations_*.dart` files

2. `ImageAttachmentPicker` introduces new RTL accessibility debt.
- In `mobile/lib/widgets/image_attachment_picker.dart`, both `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(...)` calls use hardcoded `TextDirection.ltr`.
- That is not acceptable for RTL locales like Arabic.
- Required fix:
  - replace the hardcoded direction with `Directionality.of(context)` in both announcement sites

3. The remove-image affordance is below the minimum tap target.
- In `_Thumbnail`, the remove control is effectively `20x20`.
- That is below the accessibility floor for tap targets.
- Required fix:
  - keep the visual chip if you want, but wrap it in a larger hit target (`SizedBox`/`ConstrainedBox` etc.) so the tappable area is at least the repo minimum

4. The picker introduces new theming debt.
- `_AddButton` uses raw `Colors.grey` and raw `Icons.*`.
- `_Thumbnail` also uses raw `Icons.*` for the broken-image and close states.
- These are new UI debt, not pre-existing debt.
- Required fix:
  - replace hardcoded greys with the appropriate `VineTheme` tokens
  - replace raw `Icons.*` usages with the project’s icon primitives / approved icon path for this codebase

5. Since this PR is already touching the bug report UI, please also clean the adjacent pre-existing grey text in `bug_report_dialog.dart`.
- `bug_report_dialog.dart` still uses `Colors.grey.shade500` for the diagnostics notice.
- I do not consider that the main blocker, but under the repo standard we should clean up nearby existing debt where the change is already in scope.
- Please swap that to the appropriate `VineTheme` text token while you are in this area.

Once those are fixed, this looks likely approvable from my side. Right now the correct next step is a focused cleanup pass rather than merge.

comment.body: Tightened in 73db4e4d6 — went with option 1 (mark sent on delete failure), so the guard is now reachable from production code. Updated the comment to describe both reachable paths: concurrent recovery for the same rumor, or the previous sweep's deleteById threw and the fallback marked self_wrap_status=sent.

Fixed in 73db4e4d6 — the success path now falls back to `markSelfWrapStatus(id: rumorId, status: sent, eventId: result.messageEventId)` when `deleteById` throws, so the next recovery sweep short-circuits via the idempotent already-sent guard instead of republishing. Added two tests covering the fallback path (delete-throws → marks sent + returns success) and the doubly-degraded path (both writes throw → still returns success, safe via NIP-17 receive-side dedup, surfaced via logs).

**Finding:** Relay List (NIP-65) Sync Failure.
**Technical Detail:** Logs show that for this pubkey, the app is connected to a default relay set but receiving `EOSE` with zero events. This indicates the user's specific relay list (Kind 10002) is not being fetched or respected, causing the client to look for content on the wrong relays.

comment.body: `@visibleForTesting` and `@internal` are contradictory annotations — the first opens the symbol up to same-package tests, the second flags it as internal-only. Pick one: if it's only consumed by tests in this package, drop `@internal`; if it's also called from elsewhere in the repo with a lint suppression, drop `@visibleForTesting`.

Early return short-circuits before the `Log.error` below. Net effect: keyboard errors are now silenced from the unified logger entirely, not just from Crashlytics. If the goal is 'don't page Crashlytics' (which the comment says), still log locally so triage has a trace. Move the early return to just before the Crashlytics call, after `Log.warning`/`Log.error`.

`_loadRelayVideoReplies` runs in parallel with REST bootstrap on every comments-sheet open, regardless of feature flag and regardless of whether the root has any replies. That's a relay round-trip per open. Gate on the flag or do it lazily (e.g. only when REST returns a `hasVideoReplies` hint, or only after the user scrolls).

Hardcoded `'Also share to my feed'` and `'Off keeps this video only in the comment thread.'` — both are user-visible toggle copy and must come from `context.l10n`. Add `videoMetadataReplyShareTitle` / `videoMetadataReplyShareSubtitle` to `app_en.arb`.

`'Reply to $title'` / `'Reply to $authorName'` / `'Reply to $content'` / `'Reply to video'` — four hardcoded English templates. Use parameterized ARB strings with `{title}` / `{authorName}` placeholders so non-English locales can reorder.

`error: (_, _) => null` swallows the failure silently. A permanently-failing parent fetch falls back to the generic `'Reply to video'` label with no signal in logs. At minimum `Log.warning` here, ideally render a retry affordance. (Also note this provider can't ever recover the parent until the route is revisited, because the FutureProvider caches the failure.)
Hardcoded `'Open video comment'`. No ARB key exists. Read from `context.l10n.xxx` — `DivineIconButton` exposes the surrounding context, so this can route through l10n directly.

comment.body:
investigated this on web. two root causes:

1. **blossom auth path bug**: `media_viewer_context` dispatches BUD-01 (kind 24242) viewer events to `validate_viewer_event`, which only accepts `AuthAction::List`. the correct path (`validate_blob_viewer_event` with `AuthAction::Get`) exists but is only wired for `/list/` endpoints. workaround: switched divine-web to NIP-98 (kind 27235) for viewer auth, which takes the correct validation path.

2. **three-state ageRestricted**: funnelcake API returns `null` for `age_restricted` on most classics. divine-web was coercing this to `false`, skipping auth entirely for videos that blossom actually gates. fixed by preserving the three-state (`true`/`false`/`undefined`) and treating unknown as potentially restricted.

fix: divinevideo/divine-web#348 (includes DSanich's PR #279 work)

blossom-side fix filed separately — the `media_viewer_context` validation path should accept BUD-01 get events for blob routes.

issue.title: feat(comments): revive video replies
issue.body:
Closes #4030

## Summary
- narrow this PR to the video-replies feature slice only
- add the `videoReplies` feature flag, comment camera entry point, and reply-context wiring through the recorder/editor flow
- publish video replies through the shared video-event path with NIP-22 reply tags, localized reply-visibility controls, and shared reply-visibility constants
- render inline video replies in comments, suppress bare reply-URL text echo, and add shared reply-parent context UI
- fix reply-only feed filtering pagination so home/latest fetches accumulate visible videos across raw pages instead of ending early on reply-heavy pages
- add the new reply/comment strings across locales and regenerate the l10n outputs
- clean up in-area debt touched by the feature, including synthetic comment-to-video mapping, shared event-kind constants, and reply-visibility toggle coverage

## Scope change
This PR was narrowed in response to review. The unrelated work was split out into follow-up issues:
- #4112 `refactor(camera): split recorder-owned permission flow out of #4029`
- #4113 `fix(macos): split native camera permission and recording hardening out of #4029`
- #4114 `build(macos): split debug codesigning and hardened runtime work out of #4029`

issue.title: fix(notifications): restore PR #3548 row styling and l10n on top of video grouping
issue.body:
Closes #4111

## Description

PR [#3548](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3548) ("new-notifications", merged 2026-04-29) shipped a Figma-aligned notifications redesign: a 32×32 type-icon column with an accent palette, inline `labelLargeFont` emphasis on actor names and titles, an `outlineDisabled` row border, and a localized date section header.

PR [#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944) (video grouping + thumbnails, 2026-05-05) reimplemented the row from scratch and dropped all of those styles. Subsequent fixes ([#3828](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3828), [#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007), [#4013](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4013)) further regressed the view container background, the date section header, and several l10n call sites. A separate small drift slipped the inbox conversation-tile preview color from `onSurfaceVariant` to `onSurfaceMuted`.

This PR re-applies the PR #3548 visual language on top of the current sealed-type / grouping / thumbnail functionality. It does not change any behavior introduced by [#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944), [#3961](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3961), [#3828](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3828), [#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007), or [#4013](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4013).

**Related Issue:** Relates to [#3548](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3548)

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## What changed

- `ActorNotificationRow` and `VideoNotificationRow` now use `NotificationTypeIcon` with the original `accentPink` / `accentLime` / `accentViolet` / `accentYellow` palette (`likeComment` falls into the `like` accent).
- Row container restored: uniform `surfaceContainerHigh` background + `outlineDisabled` bottom border. Unread state shows the red dot on the type icon, not a row-level tint.
- `ActorNotificationRow` uses `UserAvatar` (the placeholder-avatar primitive from PR #3548) instead of a hand-rolled `CachedNetworkImage` stack. The Follow back button uses `DivineButton(size: small)` and the `notificationFollowBack` l10n key instead of a hand-rolled `FilledButton` with hardcoded `'Follow back'`.
- `_MessageText` restored on both rows: `labelLargeFont` emphasis on actor names and video titles, `bodyMediumFont` verbs, `onSurfaceMuted55` trailing relative timestamp via `LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatRelative`.
- Date section header restored: `VineTheme.labelLargeFont(color: onSurfaceMuted)` + `LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatDateLabel`.
- Restored l10n on five snackbar / failure body strings that #3944 / #4007 hardcoded (`notificationsVideoNotFound`, `notificationsVideoUnavailable`, `notificationsFromNotification`, `notificationsFailedToLoad`, `notificationsRetry`).
- Dropped the inline `Divider` between rows; the row's bottom border owns the separation again.
- New `notification_type_icon_spec.dart` helper as the single source of truth for the `NotificationKind` → `(icon, accent pair)` mapping. Locked by a regression test so a future reskin can't silently drift the row palette (this was the failure mode that lost `likeComment` styling in the first place).
- `ConversationTile` last-message preview color restored to `onSurfaceVariant`.

`VideoNotificationRow` keeps the 56×56 thumbnail introduced by #3944 — kept as new functionality, not a regression.

## Non-goals (preserved unchanged)

- Sealed split `VideoNotification` / `ActorNotification` and grouping logic ([#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944)).
- The `kindFilter` parameter (Likes tab still matches both `like` and `likeComment`).
- d-tag / addressable-id navigation ([#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007)) and the realtime enrichment path ([#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944)).
- The collab-invite plaintext suppression in `_MessageList` and the `_previewText` replacement in `ConversationTile` ([#3672](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3672)).
- The legacy `mobile/lib/screens/notifications_screen.dart` and `mobile/lib/widgets/notification_list_item.dart` (test-only, dead code in production) — out of scope; deleting them is a separate follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `dart format` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/ test/widgets/notification_type_icon_test.dart test/widgets/notification_list_item_test.dart test/screens/inbox/inbox_view_test.dart test/screens/inbox/inbox_page_test.dart test/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart test/screens/notifications_navigation_test.dart test/screens/notifications_refresh_test.dart` — 143 green
- [ ] Manual: notifications tab matches Figma — accent palette + dot + border
- [ ] Manual: a comment-like (`likeComment`) row uses the heart accent
- [ ] Manual: grouped video like row shows thumbnail and stacked avatar
- [ ] Manual: Follow back button on a follow row uses `DivineButton` style
- [ ] Manual: long-press on system row does nothing (kept behavior)
- [ ] Manual: Spanish locale shows localized snackbar copy
- [ ] Manual: inbox conversation list shows preview text in `onSurfaceVariant`

review.body:
Requesting changes on three adjacent issues before merge:

1. `recoverSelfWrap()` still has a real duplicate-publish bookkeeping hole when `deleteById()` fails after a successful self-wrap publish. Please close that loop with a best-effort `markSelfWrapStatus(...sent...)` fallback so the row does not stay retryable in a state that republishes the self-wrap.
2. The `selfWrapStatus == sent` idempotent guard is not produced by this PR today, so either make it real via item 1 or tighten the comment to say explicitly that it is future-facing/defensive.
3. The recipient-success / self-wrap-failed queue transition is now duplicated between `sendMessage()` and `sendGroupMessage()`. Since this PR adds the new twin, please extract the shared bookkeeping into a private helper instead of locking in two copies.

Architecturally the recovery direction is correct, and I agree with the core fix for #4102. I am not blocking on the snackbar accessibility point because `conversation_view.dart` already explicitly announces the async snackbar outcome on `main`; the merge blockers here are the three code issues above.

Before merge, the follow-up tracking should also exist for:
- auto-sweeping `recipient: sent / self: failed` rows
- surfacing swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures instead of only logging them

comment.body: Fixed in `6e954c06e`. The duplicated delayed cleanup is collapsed now: navigation happens first, reply-context clearing happens once afterward, and the delayed `clearAll` runs from a single `didNavigate` path instead of both branches.
